'''''Lotus pedunculatus''''' (formerly '''''Lotus uliginosus'''''), the '''big trefoil''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=LOPE80|taxon=Lotus pedunculatus|accessdate=23 June 2015}}</ref> '''greater bird's-foot-trefoil'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''marsh bird's-foot trefoil''', is a member of the pea family ([[Fabaceae]]).

It is a [[herbaceous perennial]] growing throughout [[Europe]] in damp, open locations. As one common name suggests, it is a larger plant than related ''[[Lotus (genus)|Lotus]]'' species, growing {{Convert|20|-|80|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} tall, with [[leaf]]lets {{Convert|10|-|25|mm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long and {{Convert|10|-|20|mm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} broad. Five to twelve golden-yellow [[flower]]s {{Convert|10|-|18|mm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long are borne in an [[umbel]] at the tip of the upright stem.

Unlike related species, the stem is always hollow, and the [[sepal]]s turn back at their tips – these [[sepal]] tips form a characteristic "green star" at the end of the [[flower bud]]. The peak flowering period in the [[United Kingdom]] is June and July.<ref>[[C. A. Stace]], ''Interactive Flora of the British Isles, a Digital Encyclopaedia''. {{ISBN|90-75000-69-3}}. ([http://nlbif.eti.uva.nl/bis/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=2878 Online version] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608014232/http://nlbif.eti.uva.nl/bis/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=2878 |date=2011-06-08 }})</ref>

Lotus pedunculatus has been introduced to the western side of the [[United States]] and is now a prevalent [[weed]] in irrigated lawns and draining waste areas. Due to this it is considered a problem in gardens across the west and as a [[legume]] promotes other weed [[Plant development|growth]] as a nitrogen fixer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lotus uliginosus - Burke Herbarium Image Collection |url=https://burkeherbarium.org/imagecollection/taxon.php?Taxon=Lotus%20uliginosus |access-date=2024-08-06 |website=burkeherbarium.org}}</ref>

''Lotus pedunculatus'' occurs in a wide range of [[Soil acidity|neutral]], damp, open habitats, including certain [[fen-meadow]] [[plant association]]s such as [[Juncus subnodulosus-Cirsium palustre fen-meadow|''Juncus subnodulosus''-''Cirsium palustre'' fen-meadow]] [[habitat]].<ref>C. Michael Hogan. 2009. [http://www.globaltwitcher.com/artspec_information.asp?thingid=48639 ''Marsh Thistle: Cirsium palustre'', GlobalTwitcher.com, ed. N. Strömberg] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121213144520/http://www.globaltwitcher.com/artspec_information.asp?thingid=48639 |date=December 13, 2012 }}</ref>

''Lotus pedunculatus'' is also a [[Host plant|host]] plant for ovipositioning of the wood white butterfly, ''[[Leptidea sinapis]].''<ref>Clarke, S. A.; Green, D. G.; Joy, J.; Wollen, K.; Butler, I. (2011-04-01). [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10841-010-9300-8 "Leptidea sinapis (Wood White butterfly) egg-laying habitat and adult dispersal studies in Herefordshire"]. ''Journal of Insect Conservation''. '''15''' (1-2): 23–35. [[Digital object identifier|doi]]:[https://doi.org/10.1007%2Fs10841-010-9300-8 10.1007/s10841-010-9300-8]. [[International Standard Serial Number|ISSN]] [https://www.worldcat.org/issn/1366-638X 1366-638X].</ref>
